meta.title: Free Land, Five Years
meta.skill_frame: Find the main idea: decide what a whole passage is mostly about, not one true detail.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fifth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 7.0 on the three parts together, inside the grade 4-5 band. The load is a rule stated as conditions, then the cost those conditions carried.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.basis: Adapted from the National Park Service, 'The Homestead Act', Homestead National Historical Park.
source.attribution: U.S. National Park Service, 'The Homestead Act', Homestead National Historical Park, https://www.nps.gov/articles/the-homestead-act.htm, accessed 2026-11-15. U.S. federal government work; public domain in the U.S.
source.text_status: Adapted, reading load reduced by splitting long sentences.
source.survey: Land was free only after five years of work on it, so the price of the act was time rather than money.
source.avoided: No claims about who succeeded; no acreage figures beyond the page's own.

session.difficulty_basis: How far the stated idea sits from the words the passage uses.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The Homestead Act of 1862 was one of the most important laws in United States history. Abraham Lincoln signed it during the Civil War. The law eventually handed over 270 million acres of public land to private people. That was 10 percent of the area of the United States. To homestead, a person had to be the head of a household. The person had to be at least 21 years old. The person also had to state officially that he or she had never fought against the United States with weapons. With these rules met, a homesteader could claim a 160-acre piece of land.
passage.part_2: Settlers came from many walks of life. They included newly arrived immigrants. They included farmers from the East who did not own land. They included single women and former slaves. They came to meet the challenge of proving up and keeping this free land. Each homesteader had to live on the land. Each had to build a home, make improvements, and farm for five years. After five years, the homesteader was able to prove up. A total filing fee of 18 dollars was the only money required. But sacrifice and hard work demanded a different price from the hopeful settlers.
passage.part_3: People who were interested in homesteading first had to file their intentions at the nearest Land Office. A brief check was made for any previous ownership claims on the plot of land in question. The person who hoped to homestead paid a filing fee of 10 dollars in order to claim the land temporarily. The homesteader also paid a 2 dollar commission to the land agent. After the homesteader completed the final form successfully, he or she paid a 6 dollar fee. The homesteader then received the patent for the land. The patent was signed with the name of the current President of the United States.
